newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blames Lukashenko for crisis in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blames Lukashenko for crisis in Belarus.

text.p: The United States expressed concern on Thursday at the growing political crisis in Belarus, saying President Alexander Lukashenko's attempt to expand his powers by referendum had created "instability and fear."

The State Department called on Lukashenko and his political opponents, who are trying to impeach him, to seek a compromise that would respect the former Soviet republic's constitution and democratic norms.
The U.S. statement came as Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin arrived in the Belarus capital of Minsk, hoping to defuse the standoff.

State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said that "the fundamental cause for the volatile situation in Belarus" was the referendum called by Lukashenko, which has already begun and is due to end Sunday.
Lukashenko's proposals would give him "virtually unlimited powers" and eliminate constitutional checks and balances.
"The escalating political crisis in Belarus is a matter of concern to all democratic nations," Davies said in Washington's second statement this week on the issue.

"The manner in which the referendum ... has been conducted has created an atmosphere of instability and fear within Belarus that has alarmed the international community and will have negative political and economic consequences for the people of Belarus."

Davies said that while Washington did not seek to dictate to Belarus the form of government it should have, it was essential for all parties to work within the constitution and respect democratic norms and freedoms and basic human rights.
"The United States urges once again that all parties in Belarus seek a compromise," he said.
